messages:
Sam: heads up — mirror connector from kafka->s3 seems to have written into another customer's workspace bucket. caught by log alert.
Maria: omg can you paste the log id?
Sam: log id: 2024-10-11T09:12:03Z mirror-sync ERROR tenant-mismatch tenant_id=acme123 target_bucket=rw-cust-bkt-789 source_topic=prod-metrics
Noah: is this the mirror that runs in dedicated region B? /cc @Devon
Sam: yes, dedicated region-b, connector v1.3.2
Sara: immediate actions: 1) revoke connector service-account write role 2) rotate any KMS keys used for uploads? 3) enable audit-log tailing for that SA
Devon: agree. revoking role now. running: `gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding proj-infra --member=serviceAccount:mirror-sa@infra.iam --role=roles/storage.objectAdmin` 
audit-bot: Policy change recorded: mirror-sa role WRITE_REMOVED at 2024-10-11T09:15:02Z
Sam: thanks. quick question — how did it end up mapping to the wrong workspace? suspect RBAC mapping stage in org-routing service.
Noah: I pulled the connector config: it used workspace_alias mapping for org lookup. that code path was recently refactored in PR #4127.
Sara: PR 4127 modified fallback to use `org_id` from topic metadata when alias missing. possible race with namespace claims.
Devon: can we reproduce locally? steps?
Sam: repro steps: 1) deploy 2 mirror connectors with same alias across orgs 2) force leader failover 3) push minimal payload 4) observe bucket write target. attached stacktrace: `org-routing.go:124: warn: resolved workspace_id=org-42 but writer resolved to workspace=org-99`
Noah: that stacktrace matches a missing tenant-scoped cache invalidation. cache key used `alias` without org scoping.
Sara: immediate mitigation: patch to lookup key -> `org_id:alias` pushed to canary, plus add stricter RBAC check at write-time: verify SA's allowed_workspace == target_workspace before writing
Sam: KMS concerns: if data got encrypted with victim workspace CMK, need to audit KMS decrypts — check logs for decrypt by mirror-sa against keys in org-99
Devon: querying KMS logs now: `audit-log filter="protoPayload.methodName=\"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt\" AND resourceName:org-99"` — no decrypts from mirror-sa found so far
Sara: good, that limits exposure to metadata and object storage write only. still not great.
Noah: filing an incident: INC-2024-301, severity P1 (possible cross-tenant write). adding timeline and mitigation steps
Sam: action items
- Devon: revoke SA write (done) + confirm no further writes (in progress)
- Sara: patch org-routing cache key and rollout canary
- Noah: KMS audit and bucket object inventory for suspect time window
- Maria: notify CS for affected customers and legal if data exfil risk
oncall: acknowledged. will monitor for any alerts and escalate to SRE if needed
Maria: PSA: customers potentially affected: org-99 (target), org-42 (source). drafting notification, want staging wording before send
Sara: put a hold on automated retries for mirror connector until canary validated
Sam: thanks all. keep thread updates short. will attach log snapshots and PR links.
Devon: PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4210 patch for cache key
Sara: rolled canary to 3 nodes at 09:48Z, monitoring 5m
audit-bot: Alert: object-write-rate to rw-cust-bkt-789 stopped after revoke at 09:16Z
Sam: ending note: need a postmortem template covering RBAC config drift + recommended periodic reconciliation of connector role bindings
Noah: noted. will own postmortem. assigning to security leads
Maria: thanks team :thumbsup:
